thread:
anna.k: Quick convo — proposal: split quant profile namespace into global / customer / transient. Reason: current single namespace makes per-customer surgical overrides painful and forces runtime to do linear lookup. Sketch below.

jamal: Sounds reasonable. Do you have perf numbers on lookup cost? also what's impact on rollback?

anna.k: No hard numbers yet. Hypothesis: O(1) checks with hashed tenant id + profile id vs current chain of fallbacks. Should reduce lookup latency ~100-200us in hot path. Rollback: keep previous behavior via config flag `quant.namespace_compat = true`.

sophia: How does this interact with profile inheritance? e.g., customer profile that only overrides attention scales.

anna.k: We keep inheritance: profiles are layers. Namespace split only changes where layers are resolved. So resolution order: tenant-specific -> service-default -> global-default. We add a TTL for transient profiles (shadow tests).

mike_r: Ops concerns: migration will have to copy existing profile metadata into tenant buckets for customers with overrides. Can we avoid data duplication?

anna.k: Plan: lazy materialization. On first use, we materialize a tenant-layer pointer that references existing defs. No deep copy. We also add a background job to compact unused refs.

li: Telemetry—what signals do we need to gate FP8/INT8 rollouts? We should track token-level loss, degscore, and headwise saturation metrics.

sophia: +1. Also expose a per-profile `quality_delta` estimate in the catalog to aid canary decisioning.

quantops-bot: FYI — added `quant.namespace-split` to the RFC tracker: https://rfc.internal/1234

jamal: Can we add a runtime fast-path for "no-override" tenants to avoid extra hash checks? e.g., branch on `tenant.has_overrides` bitset.

anna.k: Yes — runtime will maintain a tenant map bitset. Fast-path if 0. Fallback otherwise. That keeps hotpath tight.

mike_r: Rollout plan idea: 1) behind feature flag; 2) opt-in tenants for canary; 3) shadow traffic for 2 weeks; 4) gradual age-based cutover. Ops ok?

mike_r: Also need a playbook entry for emergency rollback — set `quant.namespace_compat = true` and flush caches.

sophia: One more: make sure profile diffs are human readable. Add `--diff-format=semantic` to the catalog tool.

anna.k: Action items: anna write RFC with these details (+benchmarks), jamal to prototype bitset fast-path, mike to draft rollout + rollback playbook, sophia to spec telemetry signals. Target: RFC out by EOD Friday, prototype week after.

jamal: I'll start a microbenchmark today. ping me if you want to review the harness.

anna.k: thanks all :thumbsup:
